openstreetmap.usage: Road graph, cycling infrastructure, signposted cycle routes (véloroutes, RAVeL, cycle superhighways), surface, lighting, traffic direction and points of interest

ign_rge_alti.usage: Elevation of every node in the graph, from which segment gradients are derived

points_lumineux.usage: Densifying street lighting where OpenStreetMap is patchy

accidents_de_velo.detail: derived from the ONISR BAAC files, published by Koumoul
accidents_de_velo.usage: Accident penalty on road segments, France

geolocalisation_des_accidents_de.usage: Accident penalty on road segments, Belgium

base_adresse_nationale.usage: Autocomplete and geocoding of French addresses

gbfs.usage: Live availability of stations and bikes

cams.usage: European air quality index along the route

world_air_quality_index.usage: Ground monitoring station readings, complementing CAMS

open_meteo.usage: Weather conditions, 15-minute rain forecast, wind, and threshold-derived alerts (storms, hail, black ice, gusts)

vigilance_meteo_france.usage: Official weather warnings by département (storms, wind, snow and ice, heatwave…) in France

meteoalarm.usage: Official weather warnings by province in Belgium

maptiler.usage: Base maps and geocoding outside France

metaDescription: The open data behind Sécu'Cycle: OpenStreetMap, IGN, BAAC and Statbel accident records, live traffic, GBFS, air quality.

jsonLd.description: An inventory of the open datasets Sécu'Cycle reuses to plan safer bike routes: how each one is used, its licence and its producer.

chapo: Sécu'Cycle plans bike routes optimised for safety rather than distance alone. The service builds a road graph from OpenStreetMap, then gives every segment a safety score out of 10 that combines several open datasets. This page lists all of those sources, exactly how each is used, its licence and its producer.

reseau.texte: The type of cycling facility, the road hierarchy, the surface, street lighting and traffic direction all come from <osm>OpenStreetMap</osm> via the Overpass API. These attributes make up a segment's infrastructure score, before penalties are applied.
reseau.poi: The same source feeds the points of interest shown on the map : drinking water and fountains, public toilets, bike parking, repair workshops and pumping stations.

eclairage.texte: The street lights mapped in OpenStreetMap cover the whole service area, but unevenly. In two cities they are densified by the operator's open dataset : the <bordeaux>Bordeaux Métropole street lights</bordeaux> and the <nantes>Nantes Métropole street lighting</nantes>.

denivele.texte: Elevations are queried for every node of the graph from the elevation service of the <ign>IGN Géoplateforme</ign> (RGE ALTI dataset). A segment's gradient is computed from the difference between its endpoints, then weighted according to the rider's profile and whether the bike has electric assistance.

accidents.registres: Two national registers are used, one either side of the border. In France, the <baac>“Accidents de vélo”</baac> dataset, derived from the ONISR BAAC files. In Belgium, the <statbel>geolocated road accidents 2017-2024</statbel> published by Statbel, whose Lambert 72 coordinates are reprojected to WGS84 on ingest.
accidents.calcul: Each accident is attached to the graph segments within a 25 metre radius, then weighted by exponential decay with a 5 year half-life. The resulting penalty is normalised by segment length, compressed logarithmically and capped at 1.5 points out of 10.
accidents.plafond: That cap is deliberate : these registers carry no exposure denominator, so a busy cycle route mechanically accumulates accidents without being more dangerous per kilometre ridden. The penalty is also strictly subtractive — a segment with no recorded accident keeps its infrastructure score, so that poorly covered areas are not favoured.
accidents.limite: A known limitation. Both registers only record injury accidents reported to the police. Falls without a third party are heavily under-represented, and geocoding is patchier outside built-up areas. The signal is therefore structurally more reliable in cities, and a segment with no recorded accident is not a safe segment.

trafic.texte: Traffic conditions are collected every five minutes from the open data portals of four cities : Bordeaux Métropole, the Eurométropole de Strasbourg, Rennes Métropole and Nantes Métropole. A source is only queried if its extent overlaps the data we sync. Where route planning is available, a congested road becomes more costly without ever being forbidden ; elsewhere, the layer remains viewable on the city's thematic map.

bikeshare.texte: Station availability is collected in <gbfs>GBFS</gbfs> format from nine French and Belgian systems, by auto-discovery of their feeds. This layer is informational : it does not affect route planning.

air.texte: The European Air Quality Index (EAQI) comes from <cams>CAMS</cams> (Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service), redistributed by Open-Meteo, and sampled along the route on a grid of roughly 11 kilometres. It is complemented by ground monitoring station readings from the <waqi>World Air Quality Index</waqi>, published on the US AQI scale — distinct from the European index, and shown as such.

adresses.texte: Autocomplete and geocoding of French addresses rely on the <ban>Base Adresse Nationale</ban>. Outside France, in Belgium in particular, they are handled by <maptiler>MapTiler</maptiler>, which also supplies the base map tiles. MapTiler is a commercial service : it is the only source on this page that is not open data, even though its base maps are themselves built on OpenStreetMap data.

attributions.lo: IGN, ONISR, Base Adresse Nationale, Bordeaux Métropole, Eurométropole de Strasbourg, Rennes Métropole and Nantes Métropole, under the <lo>Licence Ouverte</lo>.
attributions.cams: Generated using Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service information 2026. CAMS data is modified by Sécu'Cycle (sampling along the route) and obtained through Open-Meteo. Neither the European Commission nor ECMWF is responsible for any use made of it.

reutiliser.texte: Sécu'Cycle exposes a public API. The datasets we reuse remain the property of their producers and are subject to their respective licences, listed above : any downstream reuse must respect them, in particular the ODbL share-alike clause. For any question, write to us at <mail>contact@secu-cycle.fr</mail>.
